blockers.description: CLI and dashboard report DIFFERENT scores for the SAME single clean scan: report 15/100 with 5 CRITICAL, dashboard 19/100 with 7 CRITICAL. ROOT CAUSE FOUND: the SAML IdP publishes ONE certificate (serial 109f9643...) under two `use` values (signing + encryption), so crypto_endpoints holds two rows and scan.py:480-498 emits one CRITICAL per ROW — one weak 1024-bit key becomes two CRITICALs, and CRITICAL count drives the score cap. The use=encryption row is also mislabelled 'Weak SAML SIGNING certificate'. Separately the CLI omits the SAML finding entirely despite scoring it. SESSION_BRACKET=5min is a THIRD, independent issue that merges scans under 5 minutes apart (34 certs, 14 CRITICAL) — it is NOT what causes the 15-vs-19 gap.

decisions.decision: A test the previous handoff listed as a stale pin was NOT stale — it caught a real model defect
decisions.rationale: test_identity_surface::test_weak_kerberos_lowers_score exposed a live P1 violation: the compression guard read `total_score > _ceiling`, applying compression only ABOVE the ceiling. A piecewise linear map is not order-preserving, so computed 84 emitted 84 while computed 85 emitted 71, and nothing in [85,100] ever emitted more than 84. Every well-run estate scored below a mediocre one. The ladder could not see it — all five rungs already computed above their own ceilings — which is why the fix moves the ladder by zero points.

decisions.decision: Register P2b's xfail rather than delete the marker
decisions.rationale: Every other entry in tests/skip_registry.py records an environment gap; P2b is a known OPEN DEFECT kept numeric so it cannot decay into prose. First xfail the ledger has carried, hence the new known_open_defect category. The gate checks both directions, so when P2b is fixed and the marker deleted, the entry becomes an orphan and fails — it cannot outlive the defect.

decisions.decision: Do NOT promote P2b's [20] parameter despite it XPASSing
decisions.rationale: It passed by a rounding coincidence — round(25*71/100) and round(25*74/100) both land on 18 under half-to-even — while the computed score still rose. Promoting it would encode a rounding artifact as a green gate. The property now also asserts the pre-ceiling value via _computed_score() and fails honestly at all three parameters.

decisions.decision: Fix /print structurally (don't mount the chrome) rather than with CSS
decisions.rationale: Hiding the sidebar from PrintPage's own <style> block would couple the client deliverable to sidebar class names and Tailwind margin utilities; rename either and the sidebar silently reappears in client PDFs, a regression whose only witness is the client. The early return stays INSIDE status === 'authenticated' — the PDF renderer reaches /print only via the documented auth-disabled passthrough, so hoisting it above the gate would turn an authenticated view anonymous.

decisions.decision: Fix the rollup equation with ONE shared helper across five render sites, not five parallel edits
decisions.rationale: Five copies of the same arithmetic is the drift this codebase keeps getting bitten by. The helper re-derives the pre-cap value because the model does not expose it as a structured key (it survives only inside rating_cap_reason prose as '(computed N)'), and a test ties the re-derivation to that prose so a scoring.py change fails a test instead of misprinting a client report.

decisions.decision: SAML option B only (titles), NOT C or D, before the demo
decisions.rationale: B changes a wrong CLAIM with zero count/score impact. C and D change CRITICAL counts and therefore the emitted score and the ladder fixtures — not something to slip in four days before a client demo. Operator scheduled them for after the next milestone.

decisions.decision: Exposure map scoping is OPT-IN; the cross-scan default is preserved
decisions.rationale: writer.py's _load_key_reuse documents D-03 — key reuse is deliberately a global cross-scan query for REPORTS. A report asks 'has this key ever been seen reused'; the map draws 'the estate as this scan found it'. Changing the shared default would have silently altered every report while fixing a visualization. Pinned by test_default_is_still_cross_scan_for_the_report_surface.

decisions.decision: Shared CA is drawn as a HUB, not all-pairs
decisions.rationale: All-pairs over the reference estate's 10-member CA group is 45 edges — more than the entire key-reuse graph — and would have rebuilt the spider web cleared the same day. A hub is linear in members and truer: one CA with many dependants, not a mesh of peers.

decisions.decision: Crown jewels are declared in config and read at render time, with no persistence layer
decisions.rationale: Phase 195 deferred crown jewels (Tier B, backlog 999.107) because the then-CROSS-SCAN map appeared to need persistence. The map became scan-scoped on 2026-09-14, so that premise lapsed — a declaration read at render time needs no persistence at all. The renderer had been complete the whole time. Watch for this generally: a deferral's premise can expire without anyone revisiting the decision.

context_notes: Nine commits this session, all pushed, tree clean. THE DEMO IS 2026-09-18 and the walkthrough is CONFIRMED and recorded under demo_walkthrough_confirmed — rehearse THAT, not an inferred path. FIVE THINGS A RESUMING AGENT SHOULD NOT MISREAD. (1) Scoring v3 is the story: the same estate scored 91/100 under v2 and 15/100 POOR under v3 on identical evidence, which fixes the P1 denominator blindness the oracle documented — the old 'lead with findings, the score is misleading' guidance is REVERSED and the oracle says so. (2) A stale prober image silently reproduces 91/100 with exit 0 and no warning; always verify SCORING_VERSION INSIDE the container, and rebuild with `-p chaoslab` or compose tags a different image and does nothing. (3) The CLI and dashboard disagree on the SAME clean scan (15/5-CRITICAL vs 19/7-CRITICAL). Option B fixed the wrong TITLE but the gap is ARCHITECTURAL — two finding producers with different rule sets — so it remains. Scan ONCE (SESSION_BRACKET merges scans under 5 minutes apart) and do not show both surfaces side by side. (4) `pytest -k "scor"` still misses a third of the scoring surface; select with $(grep -rln "quirk.intelligence.scoring" tests/). (5) HARD-REFRESH the dashboard after any frontend change — a cached index.html serves a stale bundle, which is why the crown-jewel ring appeared still-broken after it was fixed. The deepest lesson of the session: the ring rendered BLACK for months while the API, the unit tests and the bundle were all green — only looking at rendered pixels caught it, because the failure was a valid property holding a wrong value.
